??? quote "Dialogue"

    - Hatch. I hunt. Hunted, more like; my knees have opinions now. If you want stories, come back after my second cup. If you want to learn something, stay.
    - Split print, deep at the toe. Say it back to me. Good. You'd be amazed how many can't.
    - I've been reading my own notes all week. My handwriting's worse than I remember, and I was righter than I remember. Don't know which bothers me more.
    - Everything's ready but you. Spear's on the shaft. Torvi's sitting on Zip. When you want the Wallow, say so.
    - There's my hunter. Sit. It's the second cup, so you get a story whether you want one or not.
    - Well? Out with it.
        - *Choice:* Take me to the Wallow.
        - *Choice:* What has changed on the roads?
        - *Choice:* Tell me a story.
        - *Choice:* About Shade and Tick.
        - *Choice:* Nothing. Goodbye.
    - Down through the Reedwater Bottoms to the mud hollow at the heart of it. Step aside, then strike. I'll be in this chair. Hating it.
    - When I was young, a monster was an animal that had turned mean. You could read it: hungry, scared, cornered. These days they're bolder, stranger, and closer to the towns every season. They don't read right.
    - Why? I don't know. Anybody who tells you they know, buy them a drink and don't believe a word. I write down what I see. I never used to write anything down.
    - That's the first cup. Come back for the second. Better yet, go and earn it.
    - Ferro used to make only sculptures. Herons, foxes, a spiral of chain nobody understands. I brought a bent spear-head in, sixteen years back, and Ferro mended it like it was art. A month later I talked Ferro into a pair of hunting knives.
    - Every adventurer on the Gate Walk carries Ferro's steel now. I started that. Ferro says I ruined a perfectly good sculptor. Both true.
    - My father drove a cart between the towns, and I drove my own from sixteen. Learned the land from the bench: which fords flood, which woods hold boar, which hills smell of rain a day early.
    - At thirty-three I lost the wagon and two good horses to something in a ravine that shouldn't have been there. Walked home. Sold the wheels. Bought a spear. Came to Urbanograd because it was the only town that never asked me to wipe my boots.
    - Shade's the best I ever taught. Four seasons on the roads. Now Shade walks my old routes and finds half of them gone bad. I'm prouder than I'll say, so don't repeat that.
    - Tick follows me with a notebook. I respect his father too much to tell him to take the road. So I answer every question and hope the answers make him careful. That's all I've got.
    - Walk downwind. Always.
